name: Body
blurb: The middle of the ship: the propellant tanks, the structure that joins them, the guidance electronics and everything clamped to the tank walls.

rows.name: Guidance electronics
rows.role: The flight computer and gyros that fly the stack.

rows.name: Stage structure
rows.role: Interstages, intertanks, centerbodies and trusses: the skeleton between the tanks.

rows.name: Propellant tanks
rows.role: Fuel and oxidizer for the engines. The engines switch to whatever the tanks hold most of.

rows.name: Lines, cables & pressure
rows.role: Feed lines, cable raceways and the gas bottles that keep the tanks pressurised.

rows.name: Science instruments
rows.role: What the mission is for on Mars.

rows.name: Tank joint seals
rows.role: Cheap seals save money and fail in the cold.

shapes.name: Methane core
shapes.desc: A big and a medium methalox tank, the big one on top: methane can be made on Mars from ice and air, so the ship can refuel for the trip home.
cons: Steps in from large to medium inside the body

shapes.name: Fuel tank, centerbody, oxidizer tank
shapes.desc: The guidance ring on top, then the kerosene tank, a stiff isogrid centerbody and the oxygen tank. Delta II put its kerosene on top, unusually; the solid boosters clamped around the oxygen tank below.
cons: Heavy structure
90 t of propellant needs strong engines or solids

shapes.name: Shuttle External Tank
shapes.real: Space Shuttle External Tank (also Delta IV, SLS core stage)
shapes.desc: A short oxygen tank on top, the intertank, and a long hydrogen tank below, all under orange foam, with the big oxygen feed line running down the outside of the hydrogen tank.
pros: Best Isp with a hydrolox engine
Reaches Mars with a single large engine
Feed line outside: easy to inspect
cons: Huge, tall and expensive
Little propellant mass for the size

shapes.name: Falcon 9 first stage
shapes.desc: A black carbon interstage on top, then one long aluminium-lithium tank: liquid oxygen over kerosene with a single common dome between them, and a raceway down the side.
pros: 67 t of kerosene and oxygen for little structure
cons: Needs a cluster of engines: one large kerolox engine cannot lift it
Tall and light at the top: needs fins low on the tail
Common dome: one wall between fuel and oxidizer

shapes.name: Saturn V S-IC
shapes.desc: The biggest layout here: a long oxygen tank on top, an intertank, and the kerosene tank below, with a systems tunnel down the side. The real one was 10 m wide and fed five F-1 engines.
cons: Very heavy: needs strap-on solids or a big engine cluster
Long stack

shapes.name: Saturn S-IVB with Instrument Unit
shapes.real: Saturn V third stage (S-IVB) and its Instrument Unit; the S-II used the same tank layout
shapes.desc: The Instrument Unit ring on top, then hydrogen over oxygen in one tank with a single insulated common bulkhead, helium spheres at the base and a tunnel down the side.
pros: Best Isp with a hydrolox engine
cons: An upper stage: 26 t will not reach Mars on its own, add a second tank
Very expensive
Light at the top: needs fins low on the tail

shapes.name: Atlas balloon tank
shapes.real: Atlas (SM-65 and the Mercury-Atlas that flew John Glenn)
shapes.desc: One stainless steel tube thinner than a coin, oxygen over kerosene, held rigid only by the pressure inside. A long cable conduit runs down the side and helium bottles sit at the base.
pros: Lightest kerolox structure: 57.5 t of propellant for under 2 t
Reaches Mars with a single large engine
cons: Must stay pressurised every minute: reliability 98.8 %
Long and slender

shapes.name: Soyuz core stage (Blok A)
shapes.real: Soyuz core stage, Blok A (R-7 family)
shapes.desc: A narrow kerosene core: the open lattice truss on top (the stage above fires its engine through it), the instrument ring, the long oxygen tank, the intertank where the four boosters push, and the kerosene tank. Nitrogen pressurises the tanks.
cons: Heavy structure: 62.5 t falls a little short of Mars, stretch the lower tank
Long and narrow

shapes.name: Starship stainless steel
shapes.desc: Welded rings of stainless steel: methane on top, oxygen below, one common dome between them, with a raceway down the side and a rack of carbon-wrapped helium bottles.
cons: Heavier than aluminium

shapes.name: Electron carbon composite
shapes.desc: A small, black, all-carbon-fibre stage: one composite tank pair with a common bulkhead. On Electron, battery packs drive the engine pumps; here the two packs store the ship's power.
cons: A small rocket: 20 t will not carry a crew to Mars, add tanks
Expensive
Composite can hide cracks: reliability 99.4 %

shapes.name: Centaur upper stage
shapes.real: Centaur (Atlas V and Vulcan upper stage; launched Voyager, Cassini, New Horizons)
shapes.desc: The guidance electronics on top of a stainless steel balloon: hydrogen over oxygen with an insulated honeycomb bulkhead between them, and helium bottles at the base.
pros: Best Isp with a hydrolox engine
cons: An upper stage: 20 t will not reach Mars on its own, add a second tank
Balloon tank must stay pressurised: reliability 99 %
